5
The diameter of a spherical golf ball is measured with calipers and found to be (4.11 ± 0.01) cm.
The volume of a sphere is V = 1
6 d 3, where d is the diameter of the sphere.
What is the volume of the golf ball?
A
(36.35 ± 0.01) cm3
B
(36.35 ± 0.03) cm3
C
(36.35 ± 0.09) cm3
D
(36.4 ± 0.3) cm3

hints: Start from the measured diameter $(4.11 \pm 0.01) \text{ cm}$ and work out its fractional uncertainty $0.01/4.11$.
Use the rule for $V = \frac{1}{6}\pi d^3$ that the fractional uncertainty in $V$ is three times the fractional uncertainty in $d$ because of the $d^3$ power.
Calculate the nominal volume from $4.11 \text{ cm}$, convert the tripled fractional uncertainty to an absolute uncertainty in $\text{cm}^3$, then round the uncertainty to one significant figure.
walkthrough: Calculate the nominal volume using $V = \frac{1}{6}\pi d^3$ with $d = 4.11 \text{ cm}$: $V = \frac{1}{6}\pi \times (4.11)^3 \approx 36.35 \text{ cm}^3$.
Find the fractional uncertainty in the diameter: $\frac{\Delta d}{d} = \frac{0.01}{4.11} \approx 0.00243$, about $0.24\%$.
Apply power-rule propagation: because $V$ is proportional to $d^3$, $\frac{\Delta V}{V} = 3 \times \frac{\Delta d}{d} \approx 3 \times 0.00243 \approx 0.00730$.
Convert to absolute uncertainty: $\Delta V \approx 0.00730 \times 36.35 \approx 0.27 \text{ cm}^3$, which rounds to one significant figure as $0.3 \text{ cm}^3$.
Match decimal places: with uncertainty $0.3 \text{ cm}^3$, the volume $36.35 \text{ cm}^3$ must be rounded to one decimal place, $36.4 \text{ cm}^3$.
This gives $(36.4 \pm 0.3) \text{ cm}^3$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This copies the $0.01 \text{ cm}$ diameter uncertainty directly to the volume, ignoring that $V$ depends on $d^3$ and has units of $\text{cm}^3$.

B.explanation: This multiplies the $0.01 \text{ cm}$ uncertainty by 3 but still treats it as an absolute uncertainty, instead of tripling the fractional uncertainty.

C.explanation: This gives the unrounded volume $36.35 \text{ cm}^3$ with an uncertainty that is too small and quoted to two significant figures.

D.explanation: The nominal volume is about $36.4 \text{ cm}^3$ and tripling the fractional uncertainty in $d$ gives an absolute uncertainty of about $0.3 \text{ cm}^3$.
